- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices during low sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.2) — add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days — adjust forward by 0.5–1.5% per day for recent sentiment-driven moves.
- Avoid sharp downward corrections after upward spikes — if sentiment drops sharply, reduce forecast decline by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility — smooth out forecast extremes using 3-day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., < 0.15 over 5 days), forecast should be anchored to 10–15% below recent 18-day average, not to recent highs.
